- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment history) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment periods (negative sentiment history) — increase forecast lows.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes — cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below prior high or adjust downward by 1–2 points.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if last 3 sentiment values are negative, reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3 periods.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to overestimate early in trend — adjust downward by 1–3% for first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- Avoid “sentiment echo” — if sentiment is negative but price is rising, don’t assume continuation — reduce forecast slope.
